title: Nothing is above Him, and His signs are everywhere you look
subtitle: The Outward and Uppermost, high over all things and evident in all things
intro: Az-Zahir (الظَّاهِرُ) means the Outward and Uppermost: Allah is above all things, with nothing over Him, prevailing over everything, and His existence is evident through countless signs. It matters to you because no power that threatens you sits above Him, and proof of Him is in plain sight.

root.sense: The root means the back, the top surface, what shows. Zahara means to appear, and also to rise above and prevail: to stand on top of something is to overcome it. The Quran uses the verb for making the true religion prevail over all others (9:33). The name joins both: high above, and plainly evident.

row.title: They have the upper hand
sub: the boss, the system, the bully

knowing: Az-Zahir is the third name of 57:3, and the Prophet ﷺ defined it himself in the supplication reported in Sahih Muslim: You are the Outward, and there is nothing above You. {idea}Az-Zahir is height and dominance{/idea}: He is above His creation, over it, prevailing over it. No king, army or system stands higher.

Scholars also explained it as the Evident: the One whose existence and perfection are shown by everything He made. The order of the heavens, the precision of a cell and the voice of conscience all point to Him. He is hidden from our eyes, yet nothing in existence is more clearly indicated.

Al-Awwal and Al-Akhir describe Him in relation to time. Az-Zahir and Al-Batin describe Him in relation to reach. Az-Zahir is His being above and over everything; its partner, Al-Batin, is His being so near and so aware that nothing is beneath or beyond Him.
seeing: Allah promises: We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth (41:53). Look at a night sky away from city lights, or at the folds of a newborn's ear, and you are looking at Az-Zahir's signature.

Pharaoh told Haman to build him a tower so he could climb to the heavens and look for the God of Musa (40:36-37). He thought he was the highest thing in Egypt. He drowned. The One above all things does not need to be reached by towers; He is already over every tower and every tyrant.
trusting: Much of our fear is the fear of someone above us: the manager who decides your future, the landlord, the official who can sign or refuse, a state or an army far stronger than you. {trap}When they seem to have the final say, the heart bends toward them and can even compromise its faith to please them{/trap}. Az-Zahir answers that fear. There is nothing above Him. Every authority over you sits beneath His authority.

So you can be respectful and still be free. {reward}You take your case to people politely and take your heart to the One above them{/reward}. If they help, He moved them; if they refuse, He has other doors. And when doubts about His existence whisper, step outside and look. The signs are not hidden; Az-Zahir made sure of that.
loving: There is a kind of love that grows from awe: the feeling on a mountaintop, or under a sky full of stars, that you are small and something vast is over you. {idea}Az-Zahir is the One behind that feeling{/idea}. He is above everything, yet He fills the world with signs so that you will find Him. Majesty that wants to be known is easy to love.
now: You are sitting outside the office of the person deciding your visa, your appeal or your contract, rehearsing what to say, feeling completely at their mercy. Their desk is high; their pen decides. Remember Az-Zahir: there is nothing above Him, and that pen is beneath His command too. Breathe, make dua, and walk in.
old: The people above me have the final say over my life.
new: Az-Zahir is above them all; their power works only beneath His.
try: Spend five minutes tonight looking at the sky, and name three signs of Him you see in creation.

dua.text: O Allah, You are Az-Zahir and there is nothing above You. Free my heart from fearing those beneath You, and open my eyes to Your signs wherever I look.
dua.note: The Prophet ﷺ named Him Az-Zahir in his bedtime supplication in Sahih Muslim; call on Him this way when you feel overpowered by people.

pairs.why: Az-Zahir is above everything, Al-Batin nearer than anything; together nothing is beyond Him in any direction.
Both affirm His highness: Al-Aliyy His exaltation, Az-Zahir that He is over all things and prevails over them.

faq.a: Az-Zahir means the Outward or Uppermost: Allah is above all things with nothing over Him, prevailing over His creation, and His existence is evident through countless signs. The Prophet ﷺ explained it: You are the Outward, nothing is above You (Sahih Muslim).

faq.q: How can Allah be both Az-Zahir and Al-Batin?
faq.a: The two describe different aspects. Az-Zahir means He is above all things and His signs are evident; Al-Batin means nothing is beneath or beyond Him, He knows every hidden thing and is unseen by eyes. Both appear together in 57:3 and are affirmed without contradiction.
